subject: accountancy

concepts.title: Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP)
concepts.definition: Standardised directives and regulatory conventions developed over time to bring uniform presentation and comparability across financial records.
concepts.key_idea: Standard rules ensuring comparability and reliability across financial statements.
question_patterns: what is meant by Generally Accepted Accounting Principles in Class 11 accountancy
explain the necessity of GAAP for financial statement comparability
how do accounting conventions and concepts form the foundation of GAAP
describe the evolving nature of GAAP in response to economic changes
state the primary objective of implementing uniform accounting principles

solution_steps.explain: GAAP provides universal standards for financial reporting across business entities.
Standard accounting policies allow intra-firm and inter-firm comparison.

concepts.title: Business Entity Concept
concepts.definition: The principle treating an enterprise as a distinct legal and operational entity separate from its owners for accounting record-keeping.
concepts.key_idea: Business affairs and personal finances of the owner are maintained in isolation.
question_patterns: explain the business entity concept with an example
why is capital treated as a liability in the books of business
how are drawings accounted for under the business entity assumption
distinguish between business transactions and personal expenses of the owner
what is the significance of treating proprietor and business as separate entities

solution_steps.explain: Transactions are logged strictly from the viewpoint of the enterprise.
Capital supplied by the owner creates an internal liability for the enterprise.

concepts.title: Money Measurement Concept
concepts.definition: The convention that only financial events quantifiable in monetary currency are eligible for recording in accounting books.
concepts.key_idea: Non-monetary qualitative factors are excluded from financial books.
question_patterns: what is the money measurement concept in financial accounting
why cannot employee capabilities or manager efficiency be recorded in accounts
explain the limitation of money measurement due to purchasing power fluctuations
how does expressing physical units in currency enable aggregation of assets
identify transactions excluded under the money measurement postulate

solution_steps.explain: Verify whether an event can be stated in monetary terms.

solution_steps.action: convert physical quantities to common monetary metrics
solution_steps.explain: Express heterogeneous physical assets using standard currency units.

concepts.title: Going Concern Concept
concepts.definition: The foundational assumption that a business will operate indefinitely without the intention or necessity of liquidation in the foreseeable future.
concepts.key_idea: Assets are amortised over operational life rather than fully expensed immediately.
question_patterns: explain the going concern assumption in asset valuation
why are long term assets not written off completely in the year of purchase
how does going concern concept justify allocation of depreciation over asset lifespan
what happens to financial accounting if going concern assumption is invalidated
state the accounting rationale for carrying forward unexpired cost of assets

solution_steps.explain: The enterprise is expected to operate across future accounting cycles.

solution_steps.action: allocate asset expenditures over useful life
solution_steps.explain: Capital outlays are divided into annual revenue charges and carryover values.

concepts.title: Historical Cost Concept and Asset Valuation
concepts.definition: The rule requiring assets to be entered in account books at their full acquisition cost including all incidental spending to make them ready for operational use.
concepts.key_idea: Assets are recorded at verifiable historical acquisition cost rather than fluctuating market value.
question_patterns: calculate total capitalised cost of plant under the cost concept
find the recorded value of machinery including installation and freight charges
what is historical cost principle in asset recording
compute the entry value of an asset given purchase price and setup expenses
how are incidental purchase expenses treated under historical cost concept

solution_steps.explain: Sum the acquisition outlay along with transport, setup, and initial repair expenses.

concepts.title: Dual Aspect Concept and Accounting Equation
concepts.definition: The fundamental postulate that every financial transaction exerts a balanced two-sided impact across accounts, maintaining structural equality between assets and claims.
concepts.key_idea: Total resources owned by a firm equal the combined claims of owners and creditors.
question_patterns: calculate capital using the basic accounting equation
find total capital when assets and external liabilities are given
determine missing financial element in the equality total assets equal liabilities plus capital
compute equity of owners from business asset values and outsider claims
apply dual aspect concept to derive total capital of a firm

solution_steps.action: derive net capital from assets and liabilities
solution_steps.explain: Subtract external liabilities from total assets to find owner equity.

concepts.title: Revenue Recognition and Matching Concepts
concepts.definition: Principles dictating that earning is acknowledged when legal right to income accrues and related operational expenses are offset against revenues of the same period.
concepts.key_idea: Revenues and directly linked generating expenses must fall within identical accounting timeframes.
question_patterns: when is revenue legally considered realised in sales transactions
explain the matching principle in profit computation
why are credit sales recognised as revenue prior to cash collection
how does inventory valuation reflect the matching principle
distinguish between cash receipt and accrual of revenue under realisation principle

solution_steps.explain: Revenue is recognized when ownership or right to receive payment originates.
Match costs incurred specifically to generate revenues of that accounting period.

concepts.title: Prudence, Full Disclosure, and Consistency Principles
concepts.definition: Accounting principles mandating conservative income reporting, complete financial disclosures, and uniform procedural application across periods.
concepts.key_idea: Anticipate all prospective losses while ignoring unearned gains, maintaining full disclosure and consistent methods.
question_patterns: explain the prudence concept in valuing inventory at lower of cost or market value
why must businesses disclose all material facts in financial footnotes
how does consistency concept enhance inter-period financial comparison
what is the principle behind creating provisions for bad debts
describe the materiality concept in accounting disclosures

solution_steps.explain: Recognize potential liabilities and prospective losses immediately while postponing unearned gains.
Maintain method uniformity across years and report all significant user-relevant facts.

concepts.title: Systems and Bases of Accounting
concepts.definition: Frameworks for transaction recording (double entry vs single entry) and timing choices for financial entry (cash basis vs accrual basis).
concepts.key_idea: Double entry accrual accounting provides complete, accurate matching of financial performance.
question_patterns: compare cash basis of accounting with accrual basis of accounting
why is double entry system considered complete and reliable
explain the deficiencies of single entry system of accounting
which basis of accounting aligns with the matching principle
state the main differences between single and double entry recording

solution_steps.explain: Double entry logs equal debit and credit impacts for every transaction.
Accrual logs transactions upon occurrence rather than upon liquid cash exchange.

concepts.title: Intra-State Goods and Services Tax Calculation
concepts.definition: Computation of Central GST and State GST payable on commercial transactions occurring within a single state boundary.
concepts.key_idea: Intra-state supplies attract equal splits of CGST and SGST.
question_patterns: calculate CGST and SGST on local sale of goods
find total tax payable on intra-state transaction given CGST and SGST rates
compute central and state tax components for sales within the same state
determine total GST liability for an intra-state supply of services
how much CGST and SGST are levied on an invoice amount

solution_steps.explain: Multiply invoice value by CGST percentage rate.
Multiply invoice value by SGST percentage rate.
Add CGST and SGST to obtain total tax levied.

concepts.title: Inter-State Goods and Services Tax Calculation
concepts.definition: Computation of Integrated GST charged on commercial movement of goods or services between different states.
concepts.key_idea: Inter-state supply attracts IGST collected centrally for distribution.
question_patterns: calculate IGST on inter-state sale of goods
find integrated tax amount on transfer of goods between two states
compute tax payable when dealer sells items outside state jurisdiction
determine IGST charged on an inter-state invoice
how much IGST is collected on cross-border state trade

solution_steps.explain: Multiply transaction value by applicable IGST percentage rate.

worked_examples.question_pattern: Shiva Enterprise bought an old plant for Rs {purchase_price}. It paid Rs {freight_charge} for freight, Rs {repair_charge} for initial repairs, and Rs {installation_charge} for setup. Calculate total recorded plant cost.

solution_template.explain: Sum purchase price, transport, repair, and installation outlays.

worked_examples.question_pattern: A business bought machinery for Rs {purchase_price}, paid Rs {freight_charge} in carriage, Rs {repair_charge} in overhauling, and Rs {installation_charge} for installation. Find the cost recorded in books.

solution_template.explain: Sum purchase price, freight, repair, and installation costs.

worked_examples.question_pattern: An enterprise possesses total assets worth Rs {total_assets} and external liabilities amounting to Rs {total_liabilities}. Calculate capital using the accounting equation.

solution_template.action: derive net capital from assets and liabilities
solution_template.explain: Subtract liabilities from assets to obtain capital.

worked_examples.question_pattern: Find capital when total business assets are Rs {total_assets} and total creditor claims are Rs {total_liabilities}.

solution_template.action: derive net capital from assets and liabilities
solution_template.explain: Deduct liabilities from total asset claims.

worked_examples.question_pattern: Ramesh in Punjab sells goods worth Rs {invoice_amount} to Seema in Punjab. Applicable CGST is {cgst_rate}% and SGST is {sgst_rate}%. Calculate total tax payable.

solution_template.explain: Add CGST and SGST to determine total tax liability.

worked_examples.question_pattern: Dealer A sells goods valued at Rs {invoice_amount} within Gujarat. CGST rate is {cgst_rate}% and SGST rate is {sgst_rate}%. Calculate total GST collected.
Ramesh in Madhya Pradesh sells goods worth Rs {transaction_value} to Anand in Rajasthan. If IGST rate is {igst_rate}%, calculate the total IGST charged.

solution_template.explain: Multiply transaction value by IGST rate.

worked_examples.question_pattern: Calculate IGST on an inter-state sale of Rs {transaction_value} with an applicable tax rate of {igst_rate}%.
